```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(dplyr)
library(tidytext)
library(sentimentr)
library(magrittr)
library(quanteda)
library(readtext)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(DT)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_fulltext <- read_csv("DTS_articles_fulltext.csv")
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
bigrams <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  unnest_tokens(bigram, sentence, token="ngrams", n=2)

bigrams
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
data(stop_words)

bigrams |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
bigram_filtered <- bigrams |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_analyze <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence)) |> 
  select(sentence, id) |> 
  mutate(id = row_number())
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_sentiment <- DTS_analyze %>%
  get_sentences() %>%
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_to_token <- DTS_fulltext |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence))
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_corpus <- corpus(DTS_to_token, text_field = "sentence") # build a new corpus from the texts
head(DTS_corpus)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_tokens <- tokens(DTS_corpus)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_KWIC <- kwic(DTS_tokens, phrase(c("deaf", "artificial intelligence", "AI", "deaf sentiment", "sign", "sign language", "sentiment", "access*", "accessibility solutions", "disabilit*", "hearing", "language barrier", "RIT", "Rochester", "language development", "rylo", "disabled", "communication")), window = 50) |> as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
KWIC_IDs <- DTS_KWIC |> 
  select(docname) |> 
  mutate(id = as.numeric(sub("text", "", docname))) |> 
  select(id) |> 
  distinct(id, .keep_all = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
KWIC_to_analyze <- DTS_analyze |> 
  filter(id %in% KWIC_IDs$id)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
KWIC_bigram <- KWIC_to_analyze |> 
  unnest_tokens(bigram, sentence, token="ngrams", n=2)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
KWIC_bigram_filtered <- KWIC_bigram |> 
  filter(!is.na(bigram)) |> 
  separate(bigram, c("word1", "word2"), sep = " ") |> 
  filter(!word1 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  filter(!word2 %in% stop_words$word) |> 
  count(word1, word2, sort = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_KWIC_analyze <- KWIC_to_analyze |> 
  filter(!is.na(sentence)) |> 
  select(sentence, id) |> 
  mutate(id = row_number())
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
DTS_KWIC_sentiment <- DTS_KWIC_analyze %>%
  get_sentences() %>%
  sentiment_by(by = c("id"))
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
# Build a summary of each statistic for both datasets
# Claude helped build this ggplot, idea was mine though.
summary_stats <- bind_rows(
  DTS_sentiment %>%
    summarise(
      Max    = max(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min    = min(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD     = sd(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>% mutate(dataset = "All Articles"),
  DTS_KWIC_sentiment %>%
    summarise(
      Max    = max(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      Min    = min(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median = median(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD     = sd(ave_sentiment, na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>% mutate(dataset = "Keyword In Context Subset")
) %>%
  pivot_longer(-dataset, names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(statistic = factor(statistic, levels = c("Max", "Min", "Median", "SD")))
```

## Overall Bigram
A bigram done on all sentences in the Deaf-Technology-Sentiment dataset

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
datatable(bigram_filtered,
          caption = "Bigram of all sentences",
          options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

## KWIC Bigram

A Keyword In Context analysis was ran on the Deaf-Technology-Sentiment dataset.
This bigram is done on the sentences returned by the Keyword In Context process.

**This focused bigram gives us a bigram that is focused on sentences closer to the intended context of Deaf-Technology-Sentiment.**

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
datatable(KWIC_bigram_filtered,
          caption = "Bigrams focused on the KWIC sentences",
          options = list(pageLength = 10))
```

## GGPLOT

This is a grouped bar chart to compare the sentiment scores of sentences from all articles with the sentiment scores of sentences from the Keyword In Context analysis.

We compare the most positive sentiments, most negative sentiments, the median sentiments, and the standard deviations in sentiment from both datasets

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
# Grouped bar chart
ggplot(summary_stats, aes(x = statistic, y = value, fill = dataset)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(value, 2),
        vjust = ifelse(value >= 0, -0.5, 1.5)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray40") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.15, 0.15))) +
  labs(
    title = "Sentiment Summary Statistics: All Articles vs. Keyword In Context Subset",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Sentiment score",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
